past.company_description: Aspiring Scholars Directed Research Program (ASDRP) is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit summer program that provides opportunities for high school students throughout the Bay Area, especially those who are underrepresented in STEM or who are socioeconomically disadvantaged, to conduct high-level novel scientific research. Students participate in research projects across various subjects in STEM, including chemistry, biology, computational modeling, computer science, and much more.ASDRP provides students with research mentors and over $200,000 worth of research equipment in our research laboratory. Students are matched with research mentors who have experience in academia or industry in their particular field; together, they design a research project. These projects are not science experiments in which the results are known a priori, but rather are original research projects that expand current scientific knowledge. Students execute research projects, learn scientific reading and writing skills, write research papers on their results, undergo mock peer-review, publish their research papers in the ASDRP Communications online journal, and give poster presentations at the end-of-summer expo. We follow up with students from ASDRP to help place them into university research laboratories and industry internships in subsequent summers. The inaugural cohort of ASDRP started in summer 2018.Please see fremontstem.org/asdrp for details.

past.company_description: Extra Mile Pediatrics is a nonprofit organization that repeatedly provides healthcare to children in communities in Central America where families have difficulty accessing even the most basic care.  We believe that in order to truly lift a community, it's important to start at the base and build a healthier, more resilient community over time.  This requires that healthcare and resources are not just directed at those that are sick.  This requires seeing all children and addressing fundamental health issues such as growth, nutrition, development, education, preventive care, and chronic care management.  We also believe that addressing those issues requires a long-term relationship with patients, and a commitment and investment to each individual community.Our model is to send teams of both medical and non-medical volunteers to the same locations within communities at least once every six months so that we can see the same children and families, work with the same community leaders, and really get to know the specific health and health infrastructure challenges in each community.
past.description: * Designed and developed modules for electronic medical record (EMR) management system using PHP & MySQL for medical missions in South America
past.name: Extra Mile Pediatrics
past.title: Volunteer Software Developer
